mainTopic: Limits on taking collateral: from a guarantor, for wages, from a widow, and millstones
overview: The amud begins by finishing a discussion about רבי יוחנן, who holds that a lender who takes a משכון even once keeps its protections: שביעית won't cancel the loan, and he can collect from the borrower's children. A ברייתא seems to say otherwise, but רב אדא בר מתנא rereads it so that it fits רבי יוחנן. Next, a ברייתא teaches that a lender may not enter the borrower's house to take a משכון, but he may enter a ערב's house. It also may enter for unpaid wages, unless those wages were turned into a loan. Then a משנה forbids taking a משכון from an אלמנה. In the גמרא, רבי יהודה says this covers every widow, while רבי שמעון limits it to a poor one because of the reason behind the פסוק. The גמרא asks why the two seem to switch sides on the king's wives, and explains that each one stays consistent. Finally, a משנה forbids taking millstones or any food-making tool as a משכון. רב הונא and רב יהודה disagree on how many sets of lashes this brings. רב יהודה's explanation of 'כי נפש הוא חובל' continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why the lender keeps taking the collateral back
steps.stepSummary: The end of a ברייתא asks why the lender keeps taking the משכון again, and answers: so that שביעית won't cancel the loan, and so the item won't become the children's מטלטלין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why does the lender go back and take the collateral again? So that the seventh year will not cancel the loan, and so that the item will not become movable property belonging to the borrower's children.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting the end of a ברייתא about a lender who must give the משכון back to the borrower each day or night. This sets up a challenge to רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A loan backed by a משכון is not cancelled by שביעית. Normally a lender cannot collect his debt from the מטלטלין that the borrower's children inherit. Holding a משכון protects the lender in both cases.

keyTerms.meaning: going back and taking collateral again
the seventh year (שמיטה), which cancels loans

phrases.english: Why does one go back and take collateral again?
So that the seventh year should not cancel it,
and so that it should not become movable property in the hands of his children.
phrases.notes: Normally a debt can't be collected from the מטלטלין that children inherit, so taking the item keeps the lender's claim to it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא being brought up against רבי יוחנן
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Taking a משכון protects the loan from שביעית and lets the lender collect from the heirs.

steps.title: Inference: the rights only come from taking it again
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads the ברייתא closely. The lender gets these rights only because he keeps re-taking the משכון. That goes against רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason is that he went back and took it as collateral again. But if he did not go back and take it again, no, he does not get these benefits!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws an inference from the ברייתא's wording and uses it to attack רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said that taking a משכון once is enough. The ברייתא's wording, 'go back and take again,' suggests that without re-taking it, the protections disappear.
steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new ruling. It is the גמרא pointing out what the ברייתא seems to imply, so that it can challenge רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: The reason is that he went back and took it as collateral,
but if he did not go back and take it as collateral, not!

steps.triggerLanguage: טַעְמָא דַּהֲדַר וּמַשְׁכְּנֵיהּ, הָא לָא הֲדַר וּמַשְׁכְּנֵיהּ לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the ברייתא in step 1
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's view that taking a משכון once is enough
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא ties the protections to re-taking the משכון, which implies that taking it once is not enough.

steps.title: רב אדא בר מתנא rereads the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר מתנא says the ברייתא's wording needs adjusting anyway. He reads it as asking: since the lender must give the item back, why take it at all? The answer is to gain the protections. This fits רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר מתנא said: Aren't you adjusting the wording of this ברייתא anyway? Adjust it like this: since the lender has to give it back, why take collateral in the first place? So that the seventh year won't cancel the loan, and so the item won't become movable property of his children.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר מתנא defends רבי יוחנן by changing how the ברייתא's question is read.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the new reading, the question is about the first taking, not about taking it again. So taking it even once gives the protections, which is exactly רבי יוחנן's view.

keyTerms.meaning: you are adjusting its wording anyway
at the outset, in the first place

steps.whatToRemember: With רב אדא בר מתנא's reading, the ברייתא supports רבי יוחנן. A משכון taken even once protects the loan from שביעית and from the heirs' claim.

phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Mattana said:
But aren't you already adjusting its wording?
Adjust it like this:
And since one must return it,
why take collateral in the first place?
So that the seventh year should not cancel it,
and so that it should not become movable property in the hands of his children.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר מַתְנָא וְלָאו תָּרוֹצֵי קָא מְתָרְצַתְּ לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from step 2
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא was asking why the lender takes the משכון again and again.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is asking why the lender takes a משכון at all. Taking it once gives the protections.

steps.title: You may enter a guarantor's house to take collateral
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא learns from the פסוק that the lender may not enter the borrower's house to take a משכון, but he may enter the house of a ערב.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: 'You shall not go into his house to take his collateral.' Into his house you may not enter, but you may enter the house of a guarantor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic with a ברייתא that reads the פסוק narrowly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'his house,' meaning the borrower's. So the ban on entering is limited to the borrower. A ערב's house is not included.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
"You shall not go into his house to take his collateral."
Into his house you may not enter,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אַתָּה נִכְנָס לְבֵיתוֹ שֶׁל עָרֵב.
phrases.english: but you may enter the house of a guarantor.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן לֹא תָבֹא אֶל בֵּיתוֹ לַעֲבֹט עֲבֹטוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The lender may enter a ערב's house to take a משכון, but not the borrower's house.

steps.title: Support from משלי: take the guarantor's garment
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא supports its rule with a פסוק in משלי that says to take the garment of someone who guaranteed a loan.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so it says: 'Take his garment, for he was a guarantor for a stranger.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא brings a second פסוק to back up the rule that a ערב's property may be taken as collateral.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in משלי speaks openly about taking a guarantor's garment. That fits with the lender being allowed to go and take collateral from a ערב.

keyTerms.meaning: and similarly it says (introduces a supporting פסוק)

steps.whatToRemember: The borrower's home is protected from a lender coming in to take a משכון. A ערב's home is not.

phrases.english: And similarly it says:
"Take his garment, for he was a guarantor for a stranger, etc."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן הוּא אוֹמֵר לְקַח בִּגְדוֹ כִּי עָרַב זָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the ruling in step 4
steps.raayaObject: The rule that a lender may take a משכון from a ערב's house

steps.title: A second verse from משלי about a guarantor
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds another פסוק from משלי showing that a ערב is trapped by his own words and has given himself over to the lender.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it also says: 'My son, if you became a guarantor for your friend and shook hands with a stranger, you are trapped by the words of your mouth, caught by the words of your mouth. Do this, my son, and save yourself, since you have come into your friend's hand: go humble yourself and strengthen your friend.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא brings a second פסוק to back up its rule that you may go into a ערב's house to take a משכון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק (Step 5) said to take the garment of a ערב. This second פסוק adds that the ערב has 'come into the hand' of the lender through his own promise. Because he tied himself up on purpose, he does not get the borrower's protection.

keyTerms.meaning: And it also says: brings an extra פסוק as more support
You shook hands, sealing the promise

phrases.english: And it says: 'My son, if you became a guarantor for your friend,'
if you shook hands with a stranger,
you are trapped by the words of your mouth,
you are caught by the words of your mouth.
Do this, then, my son, and save yourself,
since you have come into the hand of your friend:
go humble yourself and strengthen your friend.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second פסוק to the proof brought in Step 5.
steps.raayaObject: The rule from Step 4 that a lender may enter a ערב's house to take a משכון.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משלי 6:1–3: the ערב is trapped by his own words and has come into his friend's hand.

steps.title: Reading the verse as advice: pay up or seek forgiveness
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא reads 'התרפס' and 'רהב רעיך' as advice. If you owe money, open your hand and pay. If not, bring many friends to ask forgiveness.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he has money in your hand, open your palm for him and pay. If not, gather many friends to appeal to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא stops to explain the end of the פסוק it just quoted, using a word-play on two words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'התרפס' is read as 'התר פס', meaning open your palm and pay back money you owe. 'ורהב רעיך' is read as 'הרבה רעים', meaning bring many friends. That second piece of advice is for when the debt is not money, such as when you hurt someone with words.

keyTerms.meaning: Open your palm for him: pay him what you owe
Gather many friends to appeal to him
Humble yourself; here read as 'open your palm'

phrases.english: If he has money in your hand,
open the palm of your hand for him,
phrases.notes: This is a word-play on 'התרפס': split it into 'התר פס', open the palm, meaning pay him.

phrases.english: and if not,
gather many friends on his behalf.
phrases.notes: A word-play on 'ורהב רעיך': read as 'הרבה רעים', many friends.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the closing words of the פסוק quoted in Step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If you owe someone money, pay it. If you owe him an apology, bring many friends to ask his forgiveness.

steps.title: A second reading: wages are not a loan
steps.stepSummary: Read another way, the ban on entering the house covers only a loan. For unpaid wages to a porter, donkey driver, innkeeper or artist, you may enter and take a משכון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another way to read it: you may not enter his house for a loan. But you may enter for a porter's wages, a donkey driver's wages, an innkeeper's bill, or payment for drawings.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא goes back to the פסוק 'do not enter his house to take a משכון' and gives a second, different lesson from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks about a loan ('כי תשה ברעך משאת'). So the ban applies only to a real loan. Money owed for work or services is not a loan, so the one who is owed may enter the house to take a משכון.

keyTerms.meaning: In another direction: a second way of reading the פסוק

phrases.english: In another direction:
phrases.notes: This is a new way to read the פסוק from Step 4 about not entering the borrower's house (דברים 24:10).

phrases.english: you may not enter his house,
but you may enter for a porter's wages,
for a donkey driver's wages, for an innkeeper's bill,
for payment for drawings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the ערב topic and offers a second reading of the פסוק from Step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ban on entering a debtor's house to take a משכון covers only a loan, not unpaid wages or service fees.

steps.title: What if the wages were turned into a loan?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks: maybe you may enter even after the wages were officially turned into a loan?
steps.simpleTranslation: Might it be that this applies even if he turned them into a loan against him?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא sets up a possible extension of the wages rule. The next line will reject it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the worker and the employer agreed that the unpaid wages will now count as a loan. The question is whether the debt keeps its old status as wages, so entering is still allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: One might think: brings up a possible idea that will be rejected
He turned them (the wages) into a loan against him

phrases.english: Might it be so even if he turned them into a loan against him?
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the unpaid wages from Step 8.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests how far the wages rule from Step 8 reaches.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the right to enter for wages still apply after the wages were formally turned into a loan?

steps.title: Once it is a loan, the ban applies
steps.stepSummary: The words 'משאת מאומה' (any kind of loan) show that wages turned into a loan count as a regular loan, so you may not enter.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'any kind of loan.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the question from the פסוק: once the wages became a loan, it is like any loan.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra word 'מאומה' (anything) widens the ban to include every kind of loan, even one that started out as wages. So after the debt was turned into a loan, the lender may not enter the house.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse teaches: brings the פסוק that settles the question

steps.whatToRemember: A lender may not enter a borrower's house to take a משכון. He may enter a ערב's house, and he may enter for unpaid wages, unless those wages were turned into a loan.

phrases.english: The verse says: 'any kind of loan.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from Step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No. Once the wages are turned into a loan, they are treated like any loan, and one may not enter the house.

steps.title: New משנה: no collateral from a widow
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that one may not take a משכון from an אלמנה, whether she is poor or rich, based on the פסוק 'do not take a widow's garment as a משכון.'
steps.simpleTranslation: A widow, whether poor or rich, one may not take a משכון from her, as it says: 'You shall not take a widow's garment as a משכון.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It states that no one may take a משכון from an אלמנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה stresses 'poor or rich' to show the rule does not depend on her money situation. The פסוק names an אלמנה with no conditions, so the ban covers every widow.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה: marks the start of a new משנה

phrases.english: MISHNA:

phrases.aramaic: אַלְמָנָה, בֵּין שֶׁהִיא עֲנִיָּיה בֵּין שֶׁהִיא עֲשִׁירָה –
phrases.english: A widow, whether she is poor or whether she is rich,
one may not take collateral from her,
as it says: 'And you shall not take a widow's garment as collateral.'

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ אַלְמָנָה, בֵּין שֶׁהִיא עֲנִיָּיה בֵּין שֶׁהִיא עֲשִׁירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic, after the ברייתא's discussion ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may not take a משכון from any אלמנה, whether she is poor or rich.

steps.title: No pledge from any widow, rich or poor
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי יהודה: you may not take a משכון from an אלמנה, whether she is poor or rich.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: A widow, whether poor or rich, may not have a pledge taken from her. This is the view of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by bringing a ברייתא that matches the plain ruling of the משנה, and names רבי יהודה as its author.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה reads the פסוק 'do not take a widow's garment as a משכון' plainly, so it covers every אלמנה. He does not split cases based on why the תורה gave this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Taking a pledge (משכון) for a debt

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Rabbis taught:
A widow, whether she is poor
or whether she is rich,
we may not take a pledge from her.
These are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא showing that the משנה's ruling in step 11 is the view of רבי יהודה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, no משכון may be taken from any אלמנה, rich or poor.

steps.title: Only a poor widow is protected, and why
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון says you may take a משכון from a rich אלמנה but not from a poor one, because returning it daily would hurt her reputation.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: From a rich widow you may take a pledge; from a poor widow you may not. Because you must return it to her, and you would give her a bad name among her neighbors.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון disagrees with רבי יהודה and limits the rule to a poor אלמנה, giving a reason for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A poor person's משכון must be given back whenever they need it, so the lender would be at the widow's door all the time. Neighbors would start to talk. A rich widow's משכון is not returned daily, so the worry does not apply, and רבי שמעון allows it.

keyTerms.meaning: A bad name, a damaged reputation

steps.whyThisMatters: רבי שמעון builds the הלכה on the reason behind the פסוק. This sets up the גמרא's question in the next step.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
a rich one, we may take a pledge from her;
a poor one, we may not take a pledge from her.
Because you are obligated to return it to her,
and you would give her a bad name among her neighbors.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view in the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A rich אלמנה may have a משכון taken; a poor one may not, because daily returns would damage her reputation.

steps.title: They seem to hold the opposite elsewhere
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that this means רבי שמעון uses the reason behind a פסוק and רבי יהודה does not, but elsewhere we heard the reverse.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is this to say that רבי יהודה does not expound the reason of a verse, and רבי שמעון does? But we have heard them say the opposite!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a general rule from the מחלוקת and then says it clashes with what we know about these תנאים. The proof comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here רבי שמעון limits the law because of its reason, so he does דרשינן טעמא דקרא, and רבי יהודה does not. The גמרא claims another source shows each one holding the opposite approach. That would make each תנא contradict himself.

keyTerms.meaning: Expounds the reason of the verse and rules based on it

steps.confusionAlert: Both תנאים agree on the words of the פסוק. Their argument is whether you may use the reason behind the פסוק to make the law broader or narrower.

phrases.english: Is that to say that Rabbi Yehuda
does not expound the reason of the verse,
and Rabbi Shimon does expound the reason of the verse?
But we have heard them say the opposite!

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמֵימְרָא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה לָא דָּרֵישׁ טַעְמָא דִקְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a general rule from the מחלוקת and challenges it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that רבי שמעון uses the reason behind a פסוק and רבי יהודה does not.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another source shows each תנא taking the opposite approach, so each seems to contradict himself.

steps.title: Proof from the king's wives
steps.stepSummary: A source about a king's wives shows רבי יהודה using the reason of the פסוק and רבי שמעון reading it plainly.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: 'He shall not multiply wives for himself.' רבי יהודה says: He may marry many, as long as they do not turn his heart away. רבי שמעון says: Even one who turns his heart away he may not marry. If so, why does the verse say 'He shall not multiply wives'? Even ones like אביגיל!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source that backs up its challenge. In the king's case, the views of the two תנאים are reversed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה reads the פסוק by its reason: the worry is that wives will turn the king's heart, so good wives are allowed. רבי שמעון reads the words plainly: even righteous wives like אביגיל may not be many, and a wife who turns his heart is forbidden even alone. This is the reverse of how they ruled about the אלמנה.

keyTerms.meaning: He shall not take many wives (a law for a king)
Turn his heart away (from serving ה׳)
Why does the verse need to say this?
Abigail, a righteous wife of דוד

steps.whatToRemember: With the אלמנה, רבי שמעון uses the reason and רבי יהודה does not. With the king's wives it is reversed. The גמרא now has to explain this contradiction.

phrases.english: As it is taught:
"And he shall not multiply wives for himself":
phrases.notes: דברים 17:17, a law about a king.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: He may take many,

phrases.aramaic: וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא יְהוּ מְסִירוֹת אֶת לִבּוֹ.
phrases.english: as long as they do not turn his heart away.
Rabbi Shimon says: Even one,
if she turns his heart away,
he may not marry her.
If so, why does the verse say
"He shall not multiply wives for himself"?
To forbid many, even ones like Abigail!
phrases.notes: אביגיל was a righteous wife of דוד who kept him from sinning (שמואל א 25).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the challenge in step 14.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that elsewhere רבי יהודה uses the reason of a פסוק and רבי שמעון does not.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא/משנה about the king's wives (סנהדרין 21a).

steps.title: רבי יהודה follows the reason only because the verse states it
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה really does not use the reason behind a פסוק. With the king's wives he follows the reason only because the פסוק itself spells it out.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, רבי יהודה does not explain verses by their reasons. The king is different, because the פסוק itself says the reason: 'he shall not have many wives, so that his heart does not turn away.' Why not many wives? So that his heart does not turn away.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction about רבי יהודה. His view on the king is not a real exception, because there the reason is written in the פסוק itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We said רבי יהודה ignores the reason behind a פסוק, but with the king he seemed to use it. The answer is that he ignores reasons we would have to figure out ourselves. When the תורה writes the reason openly, even he follows it.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, actually. This word introduces an answer that keeps the original position.
Explains a verse by its reason and rules based on that reason
He (the king) shall not have many wives

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהודה did not change his opinion. He still does not use reasons the תורה left unstated. He only follows a reason the פסוק says out loud.

phrases.aramaic: לְעוֹלָם רַבִּי יְהוּדָה לָא דָּרֵישׁ טַעְמָא דִקְרָא,
phrases.english: Really, Rabbi Yehuda does not interpret the reason of a verse,
but here it is different,
since the verse spells it out:
"And he shall not multiply wives for himself, that [his heart] not turn away."
What is the reason for "he shall not multiply wives for himself"?
Because "[his heart] shall not turn away."

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם רַבִּי יְהוּדָה לָא דָּרֵישׁ טַעְמָא דִקְרָא, וְשָׁאנֵי הָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised by the king's-wives source in step 15, starting with רבי יהודה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: a reason the פסוק states openly is different from a reason we would have to work out ourselves.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought רבי יהודה was using the reason behind a פסוק in the king's case.
steps.terutzMaskana: He follows the reason there only because the פסוק writes it, so his general rule still stands.

steps.title: רבי שמעון reads the extra words as a new rule
steps.stepSummary: Since רבי שמעון uses reasons anyway, the words 'shall not turn away' would be extra. So they teach that a king may not marry even one woman who turns his heart away.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון holds that we normally figure out a פסוק's reason. So the תורה could have written just 'he shall not have many wives,' and we would know the reason ourselves: so his heart does not turn away. Why did the תורה write 'shall not turn away'? To teach that even one woman who turns his heart away, he may not marry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains רבי שמעון's side of the king's case. He did not seem to use the reason there, but in fact he learns an extra rule from the written reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי שמעון, a reason the תורה writes out loud would add nothing, since he works out reasons anyway. So 'shall not turn away' must be its own rule: even a single wife who leads the king astray is forbidden. That is why he did not limit 'not many wives' by its reason. The reason became a separate law instead.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One, meaning the תורה
Why do I need it? (asks what extra words come to teach)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה: no reasons, unless the פסוק states them. רבי שמעון: we figure out reasons, so a reason the תורה writes out loud becomes an extra rule.
steps.whyThisMatters: This settles the contradiction from step 14. Each רבי keeps a consistent approach in both the widow's case and the king's case.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon (holds):
Since in general we interpret the reason of a verse,
let the Merciful One write just "he shall not multiply,"
and we would not need "shall not turn away"!
And I would know on my own:
What is the reason for "he shall not multiply"?
Because "[his heart] shall not turn away."
So why do I need the "shall not turn away" that the Merciful One wrote?
Even one woman, if she turns his heart away,
he may not marry her.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מִכְּדֵי בְּעָלְמָא דָּרְשִׁינַן טַעְמָא דִקְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer by explaining רבי שמעון's side, after step 16 explained רבי יהודה's side.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extra-words reading: a stated reason that would be extra for רבי שמעון teaches a new rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought רבי שמעון was ignoring the reason in the king's case.
steps.terutzMaskana: He uses the stated reason as a separate prohibition: no wife, even one, who leads the king astray.

steps.title: The משנה forbids taking millstones and food tools as a pledge
steps.stepSummary: Taking a millstone as a משכון breaks a לא תעשה and counts as two items. The rule also covers anything used to prepare food.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone who takes a millstone as a pledge breaks a negative commandment. He is liable for two items, because the פסוק says 'do not take the lower or upper millstone as a pledge.' This applies not only to millstones but to anything used to make food, because the פסוק says 'for he is taking a life as a pledge.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches that a lender may not take millstones, or any tool used to prepare food, as a משכון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lower and upper millstones are named separately, so they count as two items. The phrase 'he is taking a life' widens the rule to every food tool. Taking away the way a person makes food is like taking his life.

keyTerms.meaning: One who takes (an item) as a pledge
Food preparation, what a person needs to live

steps.confusionAlert: In this sugya חובל means 'taking as a pledge,' as in the פסוק 'לֹא יַחֲבֹל'. It does not mean 'injuring' like the חובל of damages.

phrases.english: MISHNAH: One who takes a millstone as a pledge
violates a negative commandment,
and is liable for two items,
phrases.notes: The two items are the lower and upper millstones, which work as a pair.

phrases.english: as it says: "He shall not take the lower or upper millstone as a pledge."
And they did not say this only about lower and upper millstones,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא כׇּל דָּבָר שֶׁעוֹשִׂין בּוֹ אוֹכֶל נֶפֶשׁ,
phrases.english: but about anything used to prepare food,
as it says: "For he is taking a life as a pledge."

steps.triggerLanguage: הַחוֹבֵל אֶת הָרֵיחַיִם עוֹבֵר מִשּׁוּם לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: items that may not be taken as a משכון.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Taking millstones, or any food-making tool, as a pledge is forbidden. The lower and upper millstones count as two items.

steps.title: רב הונא counts the lashes for taking millstones
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rules that taking a lower millstone brings two sets of lashes, and taking both millstones brings three.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: if someone takes a lower millstone as a pledge, he gets two sets of lashes. One is for 'millstone' and one is for 'he is taking a life.' If he takes both millstones, he gets three: one for the lower, one for the upper, and one for 'he is taking a life.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with רב הונא explaining how the משנה's rule works in practice: how many sets of lashes the person receives.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא treats 'for he is taking a life' as its own prohibition, on top of the named millstones. So each millstone is one prohibition, and the general food-tool phrase adds one more.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Rav Huna said:
If he took a lower millstone as a pledge, he receives two sets of lashes:
one because of "lower millstone,"
and one because of "for he is taking a life as a pledge."
If he took a lower and an upper millstone, he receives three sets:
because of "lower millstone," and "upper millstone,"
and because of "for he is taking a life as a pledge."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: חָבַל רֵיחַיִם לוֹקֶה שְׁתַּיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the משנה's prohibition plays out in actual punishment.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Lower millstone alone brings two sets of lashes. Both millstones bring three sets of lashes.

steps.title: רב יהודה's count: one set of lashes for each millstone
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה rules that the lower millstone brings one set of lashes, the upper millstone brings one, and both together bring two.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יהודה said: If he took the lower millstone as a pledge, he gets one set of lashes. If he took the upper millstone, he gets one set of lashes. If he took both the lower and the upper millstone, he gets two sets of lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second opinion, from רב יהודה, about how many sets of lashes a lender gets for taking millstones as a משכון. His count is lower than רב הונא's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא gave two sets of lashes for the lower millstone alone, and three for both stones. רב יהודה simply gives one set of lashes for each stone that was taken. So taking one stone is one set, and taking both is two.

keyTerms.meaning: He took something as a pledge (a משכון) for a loan
The lower millstone (the heavy bottom stone)
The upper millstone (the stone that turns on top)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two opinions. רב הונא counts 2 sets of lashes for one stone and 3 for both. רב יהודה counts 1 set for one stone and 2 for both.

phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda said:
phrases.notes: He is arguing with רב הונא from the step before.

phrases.english: If he took a lower millstone as a pledge, he gets one set of lashes,
and if he took an upper millstone, he gets one set of lashes,
if he took both the lower and upper millstones, he gets two sets of lashes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different count of lashes from רב הונא's ruling in step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each millstone taken as a pledge brings one set of lashes, so both together bring two.

steps.title: Quoting the verse 'For he takes a life as a pledge'
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה continues by quoting the words 'כי נפש הוא חובל' so he can explain what this part of the פסוק teaches.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'For he takes a life as a pledge.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line, and it is still רב יהודה speaking. He quotes the words that רב הונא counted as an extra set of lashes, so he can explain what they are for instead. His explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא used these words as their own prohibition, which is why he added a set of lashes. רב יהודה gave no such extra set, so he has to explain what these words come to teach. He begins that explanation here.

keyTerms.meaning: A life, meaning what a person needs to stay alive

phrases.english: "For he takes a life as a pledge" —
phrases.notes: דברים 24:6. These are the last words of the same פסוק that forbids taking millstones.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב יהודה's statement from step 20. It turns to the phrase that רב הונא counted as a separate set of lashes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב יהודה brings up 'For he takes a life as a pledge' to explain why, in his view, it adds no separate set of lashes. The explanation finishes on the next amud.
